title: Entropy-informed sequence-length bucketer to reduce padding and improve kernel utilization
author: Ayesha Khan
description:
Motivation: continuous batching at scale still suffers from pathological padding when request sequence-length distributions are multimodal or have high variance. Prior bucketing approaches used fixed width or quantile binning which either create too many small buckets (high schedule overhead) or accept large padding inefficiency. This PR implements an entropy-informed bucketing heuristic that balances padding cost vs. scheduler overhead and exposes light-weight kernel hints for better GPU kernel selection.

Design summary: compute a lightweight per-window sequence-length histogram and estimate per-bucket padding entropy and expected token-waste cost; merge adjacent buckets when combined entropy reduction is below a tunable threshold; prioritize forming batches that minimize expected padding cost while keeping target batch latencies within the slot SLO. The heuristic runs asynchronously in the continuous-batcher main loop and updates a small in-memory bucket table (<=32 buckets) with decay.

Key changes (high-level):
- continuous_batcher/entropy_bucket_manager.py: new module implementing histogram windowing, entropy scoring, bucket merge policy, decay and metrics emission.
- scheduler/slot_allocator.py: add soft-prioritization hook to prefer batches consuming fewer tokens of padding; supports a "pad_budget" to trade latency vs. padding.
- runtime/kernel_selector.cc: add kernel hint path for mixed-seqlen batches; when batch variance < X, choose fused-kernel schedule, otherwise choose split-kernel path.
- kvcache/kv_eviction_policy.py: tweak TTL heuristic to prefer keeping recent short-context entries to improve reuse for short-seq requests common in low-padding batches.
- tests/integration/test_entropy_bucketing.py: end-to-end harness against synthetic arrival traces (multimodal seqlen, heavy-tail).
- metrics: new metrics redwood.batcher.bucket_entropy, redwood.batcher.estimated_padding_tokens_saved.

Performance notes: benchmarked on internal perf-canary with a mixed multimodal trace (modes at 16, 64, 512). Results vs. master (quantile buckets): median p99 response latency improved by 11% (from 189ms->168ms) for interactive profile, and token-cost per 1e6 tokens reduced by ~6.5% due to padding reduction. Tail improvement is larger when modes are well-separated because the algorithm prevents mixing across high-cost boundaries.

Backward compatibility and toggles: feature gated behind runtime flag REDWOOD_ENABLE_ENTROPY_BUCKETER (off by default for existing clusters). The bucket manager exposes two tuning knobs: entropy_merge_threshold (default 0.12) and max_buckets (default 24). No breaking API changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation with unit and integration tests
- [x] Benchmark harness and perf-canary results attached
- [x] Feature-flag and config knobs added
- [x] Metrics and dashboards updated (dashboard PR in redwood-docs incoming)
- [x] Docs: inline code comments and README for module

Related tickets: ENG-5241 (dynamic-batching roadmap), ENG-5310 (continuous-batcher improvements), PM-1986 (cost-per-token objective).

review_comments: Ravi Patel (reviewer): Can you explain why entropy is a better signal than coefficient of variation for our workloads? Is there a pathological case where entropy merges cause increased latency?

Ayesha Khan (author): Entropy captures the distributional multimodality explicitly; cov only measures spread and can be insensitive when there are distinct clusters. We added a latency budget check; merges that would push expected slot latency above SLO are rejected. Added explanation in design doc and unit tests to cover edge cases.
